title: FraudShield
subtitle: An intelligent bank transaction monitoring system that flags fraudulent activity in real time using machine learning.

overview.heading: The Problem & Solution
paragraphs: Banking fraud costs institutions billions annually, yet most systems rely on simple rule-based checks that fraudsters quickly learn to bypass. False positives also frustrate legitimate customers by blocking real transactions.

FraudShield introduces a three-tier severity flag system powered by an XGBoost model trained on transaction behavior patterns. Suspicious transactions are scored in real time through a Flask API, and analysts review flagged cases on a MERN dashboard — reducing false positives while catching actual fraud.

items.title: Three-Tier Flag System
items.description: Transactions are classified as Safe, Review, or Block based on ML confidence scores — giving analysts context instead of binary alerts.

items.title: XGBoost ML Engine
items.description: A trained XGBoost classifier evaluates 20+ transaction features — amount, location delta, merchant category, time-of-day — and returns a fraud probability score via Flask REST API.

items.title: Analyst Dashboard
items.description: React-based dashboard displays flagged transactions with risk scores, feature explanations, and one-click approve/block actions stored in MongoDB.

techStack.heading: Technology Stack
techStack.description: Python ML layer exposed via Flask REST API, consumed by a full MERN stack application.

challenges.heading: Challenges & Learnings
paragraphs: The ML model was trained on a highly imbalanced dataset — only 0.17% of transactions were fraudulent. Naive training produced a model that predicted Safe for everything and still achieved 99.8% accuracy.
Bridging the Python ML layer with the Node.js backend also introduced latency. Each transaction required a synchronous HTTP call to Flask, which became a bottleneck under load.

highlight.title: The Fix
highlight.body: Used SMOTE oversampling to balance the training data and switched to F1-score as the evaluation metric. On the backend, Flask calls were moved to a queue with async resolution so the UI remains responsive while scores are computed.

outcome.heading: Final Outcome
paragraphs: FraudShield successfully completed its second academic review with a working end-to-end demo. The model achieves 94% F1-score on the test set, and the dashboard renders flagged transactions in under 400ms including ML scoring time.

title: CampusConnect
subtitle: A real-time collaborative platform where college students share resources and clear doubts in subject-specific rooms.

overview.heading: The Problem & Solution
paragraphs: College students waste hours searching scattered WhatsApp groups and generic Stack Overflow threads for subject-specific help.
CampusConnect organises academic help into subject rooms — DSA, Web Dev, OS, DBMS and more.

items.title: Subject Rooms
items.description: Students join or create rooms per subject.

items.title: Real-time Updates
items.description: New posts and answers appear instantly via Socket.io.

items.title: File & Image Sharing
items.description: Students upload screenshots of problems using Cloudinary.

title: SecureNotes
subtitle: A full-stack notes application with JWT authentication and protected routes.

overview.heading: The Problem & Solution
paragraphs: Most beginner CRUD apps skip authentication entirely.
SecureNotes was built to understand the full JWT authentication cycle.
